chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abi Hamzah, who said:

If a man is sleeping in al-Masjid al-Haram or the Mosque of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and then experiences a wet dream, and janabah comes upon him, then let him perform tayammum, and let him not pass through the mosque except in a state of tayammum. There is no harm in his passing through the rest of the mosques, but he should not sit in any of the mosques.

key_terms.الْمَسَاجِدِ: mosques, the places of worship referred to in the ruling
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: the state of major ritual impurity
key_terms.فَلْيَتَيَمَّمْ: let him perform tayammum as ritual dry ablution
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ الرَّسُولِ: the Mosque of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in Medina
key_terms.مُتَيَمِّمًا: being in a state of tayammum

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he becomes junub while in al-Masjid al-Haram or the Mosque of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person who becomes junub while inside al-Masjid al-Haram or Masjid al-Rasul صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It instructs him to perform tayammum before passing through, permits passing through other mosques, and forbids remaining seated in any mosque while in janabah.
